audience.text: C++ developers building cross-platform applications that need to generate or modify PowerPoint presentations programmatically.

capabilities.text: Create new presentations or load existing .pptx files, manage slides via SlideCollection, and save in Office Open XML formats.
capabilities.title: Create and edit presentations

capabilities.text: Insert AutoShapes, Tables, Connectors, and PictureFrames; format text at portion, paragraph, and text-frame levels; apply fills, outlines, and effects.
capabilities.title: Shape and text formatting

capabilities.text: Set core, application, and custom document properties; add per-slide speaker notes and comments with authors, timestamps, and replies.
capabilities.title: Document properties and notes

capabilities.text: Embed images from in-memory byte buffers via ImageCollection and attach them as PictureFrames to slides.
capabilities.title: Image embedding

capabilities.text: Builds on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows using CMake with automatic dependency fetching via FetchContent.
capabilities.title: Cross-platform build support

capabilities.text: Validate generated .pptx packages directly using conformance tests that inspect ZIP contents and XML structure.
capabilities.title: Conformance testing

limitations.text: No support for charts, SmartArt, OLE objects, animations, transitions, group shapes, hyperlinks, slide backgrounds, themes, or slide size configuration.
Only six Office Open XML presentation formats are supported; other SaveFormat values throw std::invalid_argument.
Cloned slides via slides().add_clone() lose their source shapes' text content.
pugixml is exposed in the public interface, requiring consumers to have its headers available.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic PowerPoint file manipulation in C++ without external dependencies like Microsoft Office or COM.
Provides a consistent CMake-based build and integration path across Windows, Linux, and macOS.

product_summary.text: Aspose.Slides FOSS for C++ is a C++20 library for creating, reading, and editing PowerPoint .pptx presentations without requiring Microsoft PowerPoint or COM interop.

uncertainties: Whether the library supports saving to streams (only path-based save() is documented).
Whether the library supports adding images from file paths or streams (only byte buffer overload is documented).
Whether the library supports export to non-PPTX formats like PDF, HTML, or images.
Whether the library supports VBA macros or digital signatures.
Whether the library supports sections (ISection is declared but not implemented).
Whether the library supports slide size configuration beyond the default 4:3 template.
Whether the library supports animations or slide transitions.
Whether the library supports group shapes (add_group_shape is not present).

workflows.name: Build from source
workflows.text: Clone the repository and run CMake to configure and build the static library using CMake 3.20+ and C++20.

workflows.name: Consume via FetchContent
workflows.text: Integrate the library into a CMake project using FetchContent to fetch and build AsposeSlidesFoss automatically.

workflows.name: Run tests
workflows.text: Build and run unit, integration, and conformance tests using GoogleTest, including cross-platform CI matrix and sanitizer checks.

workflows.name: Release packaging
workflows.text: Publish releases to NuGet on Windows using a dedicated workflow triggered by version tags.
